attempts.label: CRCNS:ssc-9
attempts.entry_title: Two-whisker sequence tuning in mouse S1 (Laboy-Juarez et al. 2019)
attempts.summary: Most of the paper's findings on single units held in this data, while the prevalence of combination selectivity and the population decoding of whisker combinations did not. Units fired more to two-whisker sequences than to single whiskers, and their combination tuning was sharper than a linear sum predicts, under anesthesia and in awake mice. The selectivity test as the Methods describe it found 318 selective response sets against the paper's 187, and was anti-conservative on a null built from the data. Decoding of combination identity stayed near chance, and the preference for inbound sequences held only in part. The awake licking behavior could not be tested, as the files hold no lick times.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Laboy-Juarez, Langberg, Ahn and Feldman (2019) on CRCNS ssc-9, which holds the spike times of single units in mouse barrel cortex during single- and two-whisker stimulation in the paper's three experiments (anesthetized survey, dense dt mapping, awake mice). It covers responsiveness and single-whisker tuning, combination selectivity, linear and nonlinear integration, dt tuning, population decoders, and the awake replication. The lick times needed for the behavioral claim are not in the files.

findings.statement: The experiment 3 files hold no lick times, trial boundaries or Go and No-go labels, so the behavior of Figure 8b cannot be tested and epochs within 200 ms of a lick, which the Methods exclude, cannot be identified. They also hold no deflection times and no per-unit recording depth (only the electrode tip depth).

The experiment 3 epochs have no deflection times, and the data descriptor does not say how DeltaT is signed or where epoch time 0 lies. The CW response latencies show that DeltaT is the time of the second listed whisker minus that of the first and that time 0 is the earlier deflection (the CW-driven peak is at 30 ms when the CW leads and at 70 ms when the SW leads by 40 ms).

About a third of the experiment 3 spike times (26 to 35% per file) lie after the roughly 300 ms stimulus epoch, up to 425 s after its start, in 5.6% of unit-epochs; the data descriptor does not mention them. The response window (0 to 125 ms) is unaffected.

The experiment 1 files hold each single whisker deflected in both directions (18 single-whisker stimuli), where the paper describes 9 single-whisker deflections; which direction the paper used is not stated. The caudal deflections reproduce the paper's unit counts. In both 20170510 recordings about half the trials of each pair that involves whisker 3 or 8 have that whisker deflected rostrally and the other caudally (about 5,300 trials per recording), and the pair 3-8 has only such trials; neither the paper, whose 261 stimuli hold no opposite-direction pairs, nor the descriptor mentions them.
Nine of the 16 experiment 2 recordings hold 16,000 to 24,000 three-whisker trials (whiskers 2, 5 and 8, or 4, 5 and 6), which neither the paper nor the data descriptor mentions.

Two experiment 2 units in 20160909 (recNames chn3 and chn4, depths 250 and 150 um) have identical spike trains, a duplicated unit. In 20160803 and 20160909 some units carry the recName of another recording than the one whose trial sequence they hold.

Two experiment 2 recordings (20160225 and 20160316, 10 units) have no sham trials, which the Methods use for responsiveness and spontaneous rates. CW-SW dt takes 101 values, -50 to +50 ms, where the paper gives 100.

paper_notes.statement: Question for the authors. The dt smoothing classifies 23% of curves as best fit unsmoothed; here the unsmoothed 1 ms curve never beats a smoothed one in held-out Poisson likelihood, and the share of curves whose likelihood rises to the largest kernel (57%) depends on how the kernel meets the +-50 ms edges (1% with zero padding). How were held-out dt values without training trials, zero rates and the edges handled?

Question for the authors. A unit whose best-combination dt curve is set constant across dt has no best dt, yet Figures 7a, 7b and 7f align or split units by it. Were such units left out (121 + 56 = 177 of 187 suggests so), or how was their best dt chosen? This attempt leaves them out of the alignment of Figure 7a.
Question for the authors. Which deflection direction were the nine single-whisker stimuli of experiment 1, and how were the rostral deflections in the files used? This attempt takes the caudal ones.

The shuffle test of combination selectivity finds 69% of response sets selective here against the paper's 41%. On a real-data null with no combination tuning the test as described gives p < 0.05 for 25% of sets, as the kernels that smooth the shuffles are chosen on the measured data. The Methods do not say how a curve set constant across dt is treated in the shuffles or how the Mahalanobis covariance of nearly collinear smoothed traces is inverted, and the analysis code is available only on request.

entries.title: Two-whisker sequence tuning in mouse S1 (Laboy-Juarez et al. 2019)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Laboy-Juarez, Langberg, Ahn and Feldman (2019) on CRCNS ssc-9, which holds the spike times of single units in mouse barrel cortex during single- and two-whisker stimulation in the paper's three experiments (anesthetized survey, dense dt mapping, awake mice). It covers responsiveness and single-whisker tuning, combination selectivity, linear and nonlinear integration, dt tuning, population decoders, and the awake replication. The lick times needed for the behavioral claim are not in the files.
